content: Lenacapavir has the potential to increase the plasma levels or pharmacological effects of various drugs by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction can lead to an elevated risk of adverse reactions associated with these drugs. The following are specific considerations for co-administration with lenacapavir: 1. Lurbinectedin: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of lurbinectedin. Close monitoring is required, and caution should be exercised. 2. Macimorelin: Lenacapavir can elevate the levels or effects of macimorelin. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Macitentan: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of macitentan. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 4. Maraviroc: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of maraviroc. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Marijuana: Lenacapavir may elevate the levels or effects of marijuana. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Mavacamten: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of mavacamten. Use caution and monitor closely. Conversely, mavacamten may reduce the levels or effects of lenacapavir. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 7. Mavorixafor: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of mavorixafor. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust the mavorixafor dose if necessary. Conversely, mavorixafor may increase lenacapavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Medroxyprogesterone: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Mefloquine: Lenacapavir may elevate the levels or effects of mefloquine. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 10. Mestranol: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of mestranol. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Metaxalone: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of metaxalone. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Methadone: Lenacapavir can elevate methadone levels. When initiating methadone in patients on lenacapavir, start with the lowest feasible dose and titrate carefully. When starting lenacapavir in patients on methadone, consider adjusting the methadone dose. Monitor clinical signs and symptoms closely. 13. Methylergonovine: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of methylergonovine. Co-administration with methylergonovine, dihydroergotamine, or ergotamine is not recommended. Use alternative drugs. 14. Methylprednisolone: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of methylprednisolone. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 15. Midazolam: Lenacapavir may elevate the levels or effects of midazolam. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Midazolam (Intranasal): Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Midostaurin: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of midostaurin. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Mifepristone: Lenacapavir can elevate the levels or effects of mifepristone. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Mirtazapine: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of mirtazapine. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Mirvetuximab Soravtansine: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Mitapivat: Lenacapavir may elevate mitapivat levels, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Conversely, mitapivat may increase lenacapavir levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 22. Mitotane: Mitotane can reduce lenacapavir levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Modafinil: Modafinil may decrease lenacapavir levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 24. Montelukast: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of montelukast. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Naldemedine: Lenacapavir may elevate the levels or effects of naldemedine. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Naloxegol: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of naloxegol. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the naloxegol dose and monitor for adverse reactions. 27. Nefazodone: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of nefazodone. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Nelfinavir: Lenacapavir can elevate the levels or effects of nelfinavir. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Nevirapine: Lenacapavir may reduce the levels or effects of nevirapine, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is not recommended. 30. Nifedipine: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of nifedipine. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Nilotinib: Lenacapavir may elevate the levels or effects of nilotinib. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Nirogacestat: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of nirogacestat. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 34. Nisoldipine: Lenacapavir can elevate the levels or effects of nisoldipine. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Norethindrone: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of norethindrone. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Norethindrone Acetate: Lenacapavir can elevate the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Norgestrel: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of norgestrel. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may further elevate systemic norgestrel concentrations, increasing the risk of adverse effects. 38. Olaparib: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of olaparib. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose (150 mg BID for tablets, 200 mg BID for capsules). After stopping lenacapavir, wait 3-5 half-lives of the inhibitor before resuming the original olaparib dose. 39. Oliceridine: Lenacapavir may elevate the levels or effects of oliceridine. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Olutasidenib: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of olutasidenib. Conversely, olutasidenib may reduce lenacapavir levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 41. Omaveloxolone: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of omaveloxolone. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely. If adverse effects occur, further reduce to 50 mg/day. 42. Osilodrostat: Lenacapavir can elevate the levels or effects of osilodrostat. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Osimertinib: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of osimertinib. Use caution and monitor closely. In all cases, careful monitoring of clinical signs and symptoms is essential to mitigate the risk of adverse reactions. Adjustments to therapy should be made as necessary based on the specific drug interaction.
